title: mojotrees fused round-start measurement plan
description: A plan, not a result. It records what would have to be measured, on what hardware, with what instrument, before any of the three round-start designs in src/mojotrees/gpu_fused_round.mojo may be called faster or slower than another. Every number under cost_model is an arithmetic prediction from the model in that module, computed by hand from its formulas and carrying no measurement whatsoever. A reader who wants a timing takes this file as the recipe and writes a record against bench/apple/schema.json; this file is never the record.
measurements_null_reason: No benchmark, profiler, build, or training run was executed for this lane. The lane was static reasoning and isolated implementation only, and a plan that carried a number it did not measure would be indistinguishable from a result.

designs.name: Materialized gradient planes
designs.statement: One gradient kernel writes grad[n] and hess[n], one reduction takes their magnitudes, every histogram in the tree reads the two planes.
designs.structural_argument: Every node below the root gathers grad[r] and hess[r] at permuted row indices drawn from the active-row permutation. The planes therefore have to exist for the whole tree whatever the root does, so no design that removes them can be correct, and every alternative is competing only for the root.
evidence_required: None to keep it. This is the shipped behavior and the burden is on a replacement.

designs.name: Tiled gradient production consumed immediately by the root histogram
designs.verdict_basis: structural, confirmed by the byte model
designs.statement: Produce the gradients one row tile at a time and hand each tile straight to the root histogram accumulation for those rows.
designs.structural_argument: The planes are still written, because the nodes below the root read them, so the design saves no bytes at all. On an in-order queue a tile's histogram launch cannot begin before that tile's gradient launch has retired, so it saves no time either. It costs one extra launch per tile.
designs.would_be_reconsidered_if: The backend exposed concurrent queues with explicit events, so a gradient tile and a histogram tile from different tiles could genuinely overlap, AND a profiler trace showed a gap between the gradient kernel and the first histogram kernel large enough to hide.
evidence_required: Metal System Trace timeline showing the gradient kernel and the root histogram kernel as adjacent non-overlapping GPU intervals, with the idle gap between them measured.
The same trace under a two-queue prototype showing the gap closed, before the design is called viable.

designs.name: Kernel fusion, objective evaluated inside the histogram kernel
designs.verdict_basis: circular dependency, independent of any measurement
designs.statement: The histogram kernel recomputes each row's gradient and hessian from the raw score, the label, and the weight instead of loading them from planes.
designs.structural_argument: The histogram accumulates in fixed point, and the fixed-point scale is a global reduction over the same gradients being accumulated. Every gradient in the dataset has to exist before the first bin of the first histogram can be quantized. A kernel that produced and consumed gradients in one launch would need its scale before it had computed the sum the scale comes from. A second hazard sits behind that one: with grid.x indexed by feature, each row is visited once per active feature, so any magnitude accumulation folded into the fused kernel would over-count every row by the active feature count.
designs.supporting_argument: Even at the model's most favorable framing, where the planes are never written and no later node needs them, fusion removes at most the gradient pass and multiplies per-row objective evaluations by the active feature count plus one. On a weighted objective it reads three Float32 per row per feature where the materialized design reads two, and it moves more bytes than it saves at every feature count above one.
designs.would_be_reconsidered_if: The histogram accumulated in floating point rather than fixed point, removing the global scale and with it the circular dependency. That is a much larger change than this lane, and it would give up bit-determinism across run orders, which is a shipped property.
evidence_required: None can rescue it while the scale is global. The evidence listed under partial_fusion below is what a narrower variant would need.

designs.name: Split the magnitude reduction into enqueue and read
designs.verdict_basis: removes a forced ordering, changes no value
designs.statement: MagnitudeReader enqueues the reduction and its readback without synchronizing, so the caller can enqueue every launch that does not depend on the scale before the host waits.
designs.structural_argument: GpuObjectiveState.magnitude_sums performs the kernel, the copy, and the synchronization in one call, which forces the round's device-to-host wait to happen before anything else in the round is enqueued. The reduction order, the block count, the shared-memory tree, and the host-side Float64 finish are unchanged, so the partials, the totals, the scales, and every histogram derived from them are bit-identical.
evidence_required: A Metal System Trace of one round showing the GPU idle interval between the magnitude kernel and the first root histogram kernel, before and after the seeding launch is moved ahead of the wait. The win is bounded by that interval and is zero if it is already zero.
MOJOTREES_GPU_TRACE=1 PHASE_SYNC totals per round, before and after, on the same machine in the same thermal state.

designs.name: Row-selection metadata on the device
designs.verdict_basis: removes a whole-path fallback rather than a pass
designs.statement: GpuRowSelection holds the selected row ids and their compensation multipliers as device buffers and applies the multipliers with one kernel, so a sampled round no longer has to leave the device objective path.
designs.structural_argument: Today device_gradients in train_gpu.mojo refuses the device path for any sampled run, which costs the run a host-side objective evaluation per round, a 2 * n_rows Float32 upload per round, and a host tree walk over every row per tree to advance the raw scores. The sample itself was never the reason: it is two small arrays and a multiply.
evidence_required: Wall-clock per round for a GOSS run on the host path against the same run on the device path, same seed, same rounds, on the machine and in the thermal state the protocol requires.

A parity check of the drawn sample: the row ids the CPU sampler draws against the ones drawn from the device ranking plane, reported as a count of differing rows per round, not as pass or fail. The device scores are Float32 and near-threshold rows can cross.
Model agreement on a held-out split between the two paths, to the Float32 tolerance the GPU trainer already documents.

designs.name: Device-side leaf assignment for every row
designs.verdict_basis: closes the one thing blocking bagging from the device round
designs.statement: GpuTreeRouter assigns every row a leaf of the grown tree on the device and advances every row's raw score, so a bagged tree no longer needs a host tree walk over all rows.
designs.structural_argument: Bagging updates every row's raw score after every tree, in bag or not, and the leaf-range update covers only in-bag rows. That, and not the sample, is what kept bagging off the device round. The router adds no arithmetic: it composes _append_tree and _leaf_kernel from gpu_predict.mojo over the histogram builder's own binned matrix with GpuObjectiveState.update_raw, so the routing rule is not duplicated a sixth time and no second copy of the dataset is uploaded.
designs.parity_note: Routing is exact rather than approximate. Both this walk and the host's tree.predict_row decide on integer bins, so they take identical branches for every row; only the Float32 carrier of the added value differs, which is the device path's documented precision everywhere else. A bag depends on no gradient, so unlike GOSS there is no sampling caveat at all.
designs.cost_note: One launch and n_rows * depth bin reads per tree, against one launch per leaf over in-bag rows only for the range update. For an unbagged tree the ranges already cover every row and remain the cheaper path; this is for the bagged tree, whose alternative today is a host walk that also drags the objective back onto the host.
evidence_required: Predictions from a bagged GPU run against a bagged CPU run at equal seed, fraction, frequency, and rounds. Because the bag and the routing are both exact, this should agree to the Float32 tolerance the GPU trainer already documents, and a larger gap means a real defect rather than precision.
Per-tree wall clock for the router against the leaf-range update on an unbagged run, to confirm the ranges stay the cheaper path there and the router is not made the default.
Per-round wall clock for a bagged run, device round against the host-gradient fallback it replaces.

designs.name: Interleaved gradient and hessian plane
designs.verdict_basis: the transaction halving is unconditional; only the wall clock it buys is not
designs.statement: Store the two derivatives as one interleaved plane so a row's pair is gh[2r] and gh[2r+1], eight aligned bytes inside one cache line, instead of two four-byte loads from two planes n_rows apart.
designs.structural_argument: Below the root the row indices are a permutation, so the derivative reads are a gather: a warp of 32 threads touches up to 32 cache lines in the gradient plane and 32 more in the hessian plane. Interleaved, each thread's pair is inside one line, so the same warp touches 32 lines instead of 64. That halving holds whether the accesses hit or miss: on a miss it halves the lines fetched from memory, on a hit it halves the lookups. The root is the one node where it is neutral rather than a win, since the unbagged root's permutation is the identity and both layouts coalesce.
designs.correction: An earlier draft of this plan said the case rested entirely on a memory-bandwidth counter reading. That was overstated. The transaction count halves unconditionally; what the counter decides is how much wall clock that is worth at a given shape, which is a different and smaller question.
designs.implementation_note: Built additively in gpu_gradient_stream.mojo rather than by editing the histogram kernels in gpu_active_rows.mojo, which belong to another lane and were mid-flight. The two accumulation kernels are those kernels with exactly two lines changed, the two derivative loads; the reduction and zeroing kernels are imported and reused rather than copied. Selected by MOJOTREES_GPU_GRAD_LAYOUT=interleaved, defaulting to the shipped split layout, so both layouts are runnable from one build, which is what comparing them requires.
designs.costs: 8 * n_rows bytes of device memory for the plane, and one 16 * n_rows byte pack pass per round to fill it. The pack is paid once per round against a gather paid once per (node, feature); at fifty features and six histogram passes per tree it is under one percent of what it reorganizes. It disappears entirely if the derivative kernels are taught to write pairs directly, which is a change to gpu_objectives_native.mojo.
evidence_required: Bit-identity of the histograms built both ways on the same gradients. The pack is a pure copy and the accumulation is unchanged, so any difference at all is a defect, not a precision result. This is the first thing to check and it needs no timing.

Per-node GPU duration for the histogram kernel, split against interleaved, at a node below the root where the permutation is genuinely scattered. The root is expected to be neutral and is not the test.
The same at two feature counts an order of magnitude apart, since the number of times the planes are re-read is the feature count.
Bytes read from device memory by the histogram kernel in both layouts, which is what turns the transaction argument into a wall-clock one.

cost_model.units: bytes issued by kernels, reads plus writes, for one tree's round start plus its root histogram
assumptions: No cache is modeled. The question fusion asks is whether re-reading the derivative planes once per feature costs anything, and a model that assumed those reads were served from cache would answer the question by assumption. Read the numbers as an upper bound and as a ratio between designs.
The fused design is modeled at its ceiling: it is credited with never writing the derivative planes, which no real tree can be, since every node below the root reads them.
The atomic strategy's global read-modify-write traffic is not modeled; its partial term is the one-tile output write.
Tile counts are the values derive_tiling in gpu_tiling.mojo resolves for a device reporting ten multiprocessors, restated here as an input rather than queried.

streamed.note: Identical bytes by construction. The extra launch is the finding.

tree_amortization.description: The shapes above cover the root only. A tree builds the root and then, for every split, only the smaller child, so the rows scanned across a tree are roughly the root's plus one root-sized pass per level. The round start is paid once per tree, so its share falls by that factor.
tree_amortization.measured_null_reason: The passes-per-tree factor is an assumption about tree shape, not a measurement. A real run would report the rows actually scanned from the leaf ranges.

phase_timers.what_it_answers: How much of a round is spent waiting rather than computing, which is the only quantity the deferred-magnitude split can move.
phase_timers.what_it_cannot_answer: Bytes moved. It counts host-observed intervals, not memory traffic.

gpu_counters.instrument: Xcode Instruments, Metal System Trace, plus a GPU capture for per-kernel counters
counters_of_interest: per-kernel GPU duration for the gradient kernel, the magnitude kernel, and the root histogram kernel
idle intervals between consecutive kernels of one round
bytes read from device memory by the root histogram kernel, which is the one number the cost model refuses to assume
gpu_counters.why_it_is_required: Every design comparison in this file that is not settled structurally reduces to what fraction of the derivative-plane re-reads reach memory. Nothing in the source can answer that.

environment_switches: MOJOTREES_GPU_OBJECTIVE=host|device, to run the same configuration on both gradient sources
MOJOTREES_GPU_HIST_STRATEGY=atomic|tiled, so a comparison is not silently made across two accumulation strategies
MOJOTREES_GPU_BLOCK_THREADS and MOJOTREES_GPU_ROW_TILE, pinned rather than derived, so two runs share a launch geometry

procedure: Follow docs/APPLE_GPU_BENCHMARK_PROTOCOL.md in full: idle gate, repetitions, cooldown, and the quality result that decides whether a run counts at all. This plan adds workloads to that protocol and replaces none of it.
Pin the launch geometry with the environment switches above before comparing any two configurations. A comparison across two derived tilings measures the policy, not the design.
For every shape, run the materialized path as the baseline first, in both gradient sources, so that a later device-path number has a same-session baseline rather than a remembered one.
Capture the GPU trace on one representative round per shape, not on the whole fit. The question is the shape of a round, and a whole-fit capture buries it.

Write the timings into a record against bench/apple/schema.json, with every quantity this plan predicted left as a prediction and every measured quantity carrying its own field. Never overwrite a prediction with a measurement in this file.

acceptance.claim: The deferred magnitude split is worth keeping.
acceptance.decided_by: The GPU idle interval between the magnitude readback and the first root histogram kernel, measured before the split.
acceptance.threshold: Keep only if that interval exceeds the cost of one seeding launch on the same machine. If it is already zero the split is neutral and should be kept only for the ordering freedom it gives, not for a speed claim.

acceptance.claim: Row selection belongs on the device.
acceptance.decided_by: Per-round wall clock for a GOSS run, device path against host path, at equal rounds and equal seed.
acceptance.threshold: Keep if the device path is faster at any shape in this plan and no shape regresses, and only after the sample-difference count per round is reported. A speedup that comes with an unreported sample difference is not a result.

acceptance.claim: Row bagging may take the device round.
acceptance.decided_by: Prediction agreement between a bagged GPU run and a bagged CPU run at equal seed, fraction, frequency, and rounds.
acceptance.threshold: Ship only on agreement to the Float32 tolerance the GPU trainer already documents. Both the bag and the routing are exact, so a larger gap is a defect and not a precision result. This widens which configurations take the device path, so the check gates the device_gradients change, not just the router.

acceptance.claim: The interleaved derivative plane is correct.
acceptance.decided_by: Bit-identity of histograms built both ways from the same gradients, on the same build, switched with MOJOTREES_GPU_GRAD_LAYOUT.
acceptance.threshold: Any difference is a defect. The pack is a pure Float32 copy and the accumulation order, rounding, and atomics are unchanged, so there is no tolerance to allow here.

acceptance.claim: The interleaved derivative plane should become the default.
acceptance.decided_by: Per-node histogram kernel duration at a node below the root, split against interleaved, at two feature counts an order of magnitude apart, plus bytes read from device memory in both layouts.
acceptance.threshold: Flip the default only if the interleaved layout wins at both feature counts and the root does not regress. The transaction count halves either way, so a null result means the gather was not the bottleneck at that shape, not that the layout is wrong; record it as such rather than as a refutation.

acceptance.claim: Any fusion of the objective into the histogram.
acceptance.threshold: Refused on the circular dependency between the fixed-point scale and the gradients it quantizes, which no measurement can move. Reopening it requires changing how histograms accumulate, not a benchmark.

prohibitions: No number in this file may be quoted as a measurement. Every one of them is arithmetic from a model whose assumptions are listed above.
No design may be called faster than another on the strength of this plan alone.
A run that fails the protocol's idle gate or quality result produces no number here, not a caveated one.
Absence of a measurement is stated, never zeroed and never estimated.
